-- Schema for database: rschema_0417

CREATE TABLE `user` (
  `user_id` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `user_name` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `email` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `password` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `avatar_link` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `registration_date` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`user_id`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `post` (
  `post_id` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `title` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `content` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `category_belonging` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `posting_user` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `posting_time` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `status` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `reply_count` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `like_count` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `favorite_count` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`post_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `post_ibfk_posting_user` FOREIGN KEY (`posting_user`) REFERENCES `user` (`user_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `post_ibfk_category_belonging` FOREIGN KEY (`category_belonging`) REFERENCES `category` (`category_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `comment` (
  `comment_id` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `comment_content` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `posting_user` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `like_count` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `reply_count` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `posting_time` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`comment_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `comment_ibfk_posting_user` FOREIGN KEY (`posting_user`) REFERENCES `user` (`user_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `category` (
  `category_id` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `category_name` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`category_id`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `notification_information` (
  `message_number` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `notification_content` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`message_number`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `comment_reply` (
  `comment_id` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `reply_comment_id` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`comment_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `comment_reply_ibfk_reply_comment_id` FOREIGN KEY (`reply_comment_id`) REFERENCES `comment` (`comment_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `comment_reply_ibfk_comment_id` FOREIGN KEY (`comment_id`) REFERENCES `comment` (`comment_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `comment_post` (
  `comment_id` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `post_id` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`comment_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `comment_post_ibfk_post_id` FOREIGN KEY (`post_id`) REFERENCES `post` (`post_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `comment_post_ibfk_comment_id` FOREIGN KEY (`comment_id`) REFERENCES `comment` (`comment_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `notification_distribution` (
  `notification_message_number` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `user_id` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `read_status` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`user_id`, `notification_message_number`),
  CONSTRAINT `notification_distribution_ibfk_user_id` FOREIGN KEY (`user_id`) REFERENCES `user` (`user_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `notification_distribution_ibfk_notification_message_number` FOREIGN KEY (`notification_message_number`) REFERENCES `notification_information` (`message_number`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;
gold_question: Business requirement description for the forum management system: The forum management system is used to manage users, posts, comments, categories, and notification information. The system contains multiple users, each user has a user ID, username, email, password, avatar link, and registration date. The system records multiple posts, each post has a post ID, title, content, category, posting user, posting time, status, reply count, like count, and favorite count, where the posting user is associated with the user ID of the user, and the category is associated with the category ID of the category. The system also records multiple comments, each comment has a comment ID, comment content, posting user, like count, reply count, and posting time, where the posting user is associated with the user ID of the user. The system supports nested replies for comments, each comment can reply to other comments or posts. The system also contains multiple categories, each category has a category ID and category name, used for categorizing and managing posts. The system records notification information, each notification has a message number and notification content, and is associated with the user, recording the user's read status. The system realizes comprehensive management of various forum information through user table, post table, comment table, category table, and notification information table, ensuring data integrity and traceability.
nl_text: The rschema_0417 database is designed to manage a social media platform where users can create and share posts, comments, and replies. The database consists of eight tables: user, post, comment, category, notification_information, comment_reply, comment_post, and notification_distribution. The user table stores information about each user, including their unique user ID, name, email, password, avatar link, and registration date. The post table stores details about each post, such as its ID, title, content, category, posting user, posting time, status, reply count, and like and favorite counts. The category table contains a list of available categories, identified by their unique category ID and name. The notification_information table stores notification messages, identified by a unique message number. The comment table stores comments made by users, including their content, posting user, like count, reply count, and posting time. The comment_reply table links comments to their replies, while the comment_post table links comments to the posts they belong to. The notification_distribution table tracks the distribution of notifications to users, including the notification message number, user ID, and read status. The relationships between these tables are established through foreign keys, which ensure that when a user is deleted, all their posts, comments, and notifications are also deleted, and when a post or comment is deleted, all related comments and replies are also deleted.
